title: How Billie became "Lady Day" and Lester became "Pres"
summary: Jones says the name Lady Day began on a Baltimore bus when Lester mocked Jones's defense of a lady, and Billie named Lester Pres.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: The reason I asked you that, Jo, was to get back to Billie Holiday. I have heard and I just want to clear it for the record because I'm sure you were there, that Billie Holiday named Lester Young "Pres" and that he named her "Lady Day". Now do you have any things to say about that?

I will tell you the truth about that. How Lady Day become known as Lady Day, it started in Baltimore and this was a personal thing. I was always Little Lord Fauntleroy. We were leaving the Royal Theatre and you know how we used to go in the back to get the food, in the house. So we were sitting in the bus to get the food and Freddie Green was sitting with Lady Day. Some guys were having fun. They had been on Pennsylvania Avenue and they come in and they was using all kind of language. I said, "Wait a minute. You guys can't do that. There's a lady present." So Lester Young and Buck Clayton always sat in the back of the bus, so Lester busts out laughing and says, "What do you mean, lady?" I said, "There's a lady in here. You guys can't do that." So right away he says, "Lady Day." Then when he went to Claude Clark Monroe's Uptown House, he started saying, "Come on, Lady; come on, Lady," and he started saying Lady Day. Then when she named him "Pres" -

She named him "Pres" because he said, "She is the President," because she said that Lester was next to F.D.R. He was the President. F.D.R. wasn't the President; this is the President, because few people knew this about Lester. Forget about his color, the complexion of his skin. He was born in Mississippi.
